h1: The 8 Best Laptop Charging Carts for Classrooms of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Classroom Charging Carts: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: eight laptop charging carts for classrooms, from 16 to 32 devices, compared on locks, ventilation, power protection and price.
summary: The Meteteel 20-device cart is our pick for a typical classroom, arriving 95% pre-assembled with independent front and back locks. The VEVOR 16-device cart suits unattended rooms, the POCHAR 30-device K-12 cart covers large rosters, and the Kraftgen open cart prioritizes quick access.
intro: A charging cart fails in a classroom for boring reasons: a roster that outgrew the bays, a lock that sits on only one side, or a power strip that trips when twenty devices draw at once. Capacity and security get the headlines, but power protection and slot size decide whether the cart still works in October.

We reviewed eight carts from 16 to 32 devices and ranked them on the spec sheets: capacity, locking, device size limits, ventilation and electrical protection. Where the listing does not state something, such as a weight rating, we do not guess.

products.name: Meteteel Fully Assembled 20 Device Laptop Charging Cart for School (Black)
products.verdict: A 20-device cart that is ready for day-one handout.
products.description:
This Meteteel cart holds 20 devices, arrives 95% pre-assembled and has independent front and back locks. The steel frame is ventilated for all-day charging.

It leads because the capacity fits the common 18 to 22 student room and little assembly is left. Compared with the 18-device Meteteel below, you get two more slots at the same $200-500 bracket.

Best for a typical classroom that wants a ready cart. Check slot dimensions for thicker devices on the live listing.

products.name: VEVOR 16 Device Charging Station with Lock & Key, Mobile Charging Cart
products.verdict: A locked 16-device cart with built-in surge protection.
products.description:
The VEVOR holds 16 devices up to 15.6 inch screens, with a lock and key, built-in surge protection, an integrated power strip and two locking casters.

Second place reflects its smaller capacity: it holds four fewer devices than the Meteteel 20 yet covers larger 15.6 inch laptops. Surge protection is the notable plus.

Best for rooms where the cart sits unattended. Smaller classes only.

products.name: POCHAR 30 Devices 14'' Screen Laptop Charging Cart for K-12 Classrooms
products.verdict: A 30-device cart with circuit breaker and grounding protection.
products.description:
This POCHAR holds 30 devices with up to 14 inch screens, has an open-back cooling design, a circuit breaker with grounding protection and two locking casters. It ships flat-packed.

It ranks third because flat-pack shipping means assembly work, unlike the pre-assembled Meteteel. In return you get 30 slots and electrical protection.

Best for larger classes or two sections sharing one cart. Budget time for assembly.

products.name: Meteteel Fully Assembled 18 Device Laptop Charging Cart for School (Black)
products.verdict: An 18-device cart that draws from a single wall outlet.
products.description:
This Meteteel fits 18 devices in slots capped at 14 inch screens and 1.4 inches of thickness, draws from a single wall outlet and uses zig-zag cable dividers with star-pattern ventilation.

It sits fourth because the 20-device sibling offers more slots for the same $200-500 bracket. The single outlet draw is simple for older classrooms.

Best for rosters near 18. Thicker devices will not fit the 1.4 inch limit.

products.name: Plugsharge 32-Device Laptop Charging Cart for Chromebooks, iPad & Tablets
products.verdict: The highest-capacity cart here at 32 devices.
products.description:
The Plugsharge holds 32 devices up to 15.6 inch screens, with surge and ground fault protection, 32 individual cable organizers and numbered slots on an open rack.

It ranks fifth because the open rack offers less security than the locked carts above. It wins on capacity and screen size.

Best for oversized rosters or two classes sharing a cart. Add your own security plan.

products.name: POCHAR 30 Unit Device Charging Station for Chromebook, iPad, 14'' Laptop
products.verdict: A locked 30-bay cart rated for mixed devices.
products.description:
This POCHAR fits 30 devices with a cap of 14 inch screens and 1.5 inches of depth, rated for a mixed fleet. It has numbered bays, removable doors and four keys total, two per lock.

It ranks sixth because it lists no electrical protection, unlike the other POCHAR above. The mixed-fleet rating and locks are its pitch.

Best for classrooms mixing Chromebooks, iPads and laptops. Confirm power protection on the listing.
products.idealFor: Mixed Chromebook, iPad and laptop fleets.

products.name: ALT Technology 30-Bay Mobile School Charging Cart Station for Chromebook, Tablet
products.verdict: A 32-device cart with UL-approved power strips.
products.description:
The ALT cart holds 32 devices across two shelves with a separate cable shelf, UL-approved power strips and slots of 1 by 14 by 10.5 inches for laptops up to 14 inches.

It ranks seventh because the title says 30 bays but the listing states 32, a mismatch worth checking. The UL-approved strips are the plus.

Best for buyers comparing 30-bay carts. Confirm bay count before ordering.

products.name: Kraftgen 16-Bay Open Charging Cart for Chromebooks, Laptops, Tablets & iPads
products.verdict: A lower-cost open cart for fast daily access.
products.description:
The Kraftgen holds 16 devices in an open design with UL-listed power strips, 3 inch non-marring casters, removable dividers, padded shelves and rear cable clips.

It ranks last because open design means no lock, which suits only some rooms. It costs less, in the $100-200 bracket.

Best for classrooms that value quick daily access over lockup. Do not leave it unattended.

whatMatters.detail: Capacity is how many devices fit in one cart. Match it to your roster and add a few spare slots for growth. Check the bay count in the listing, since titles and specs sometimes differ.
A locked cart protects devices overnight. Independent front and back locks let you secure both sides. Look for a lock and key in the title or bullets.
Charging dozens of devices draws heavy current. Surge protection, circuit breakers and UL-listed strips reduce risk. Check what the listing names.
Each slot has a maximum screen size and thickness, such as 14 inches and 1.4 inches. A thick case can stop a device fitting. Measure your device with its case.
Pre-assembled carts are ready on delivery, while flat-pack carts need hours of building. Check the listing for assembly percent.

howToChoose.note: Most schools should default to locked unless the room is always supervised.

faq.q: How many devices should a cart hold?
faq.a: Match your largest class plus a few spare slots. Options here range from 16 to 32.
Ignoring slot thickness. The Meteteel 18 limits devices to 1.4 inches thick.

faq.q: Is a locked cart worth it?
faq.a: For unattended rooms, yes. The VEVOR and Meteteel 20 are the locked picks.

faq.q: How do I set one up?
faq.a: The Meteteel 20 is 95% pre-assembled, while the POCHAR ships flat-packed. Follow the maker's manual.

faq.q: How do I keep it running?
faq.a: Keep vents clear and cables organized. Numbered slots and cable organizers help.

faq.q: Can I mix Chromebooks and iPads?
faq.a: The POCHAR 30 Unit is rated for a mixed fleet. Check others on the listing.

finalTake: The Meteteel 20 is the safest buy for a typical classroom, with 20 slots and two locks. Pick the VEVOR for unattended rooms, the POCHAR 30 K-12 for large rosters and the Kraftgen for supervised, fast access. Always verify bay count and slot size before ordering.
